analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The supplied patch bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and adds a documentation section around head lines 956-986 describing a startup shape warmup (ModelCalibrationPolicy.shapeWarmup). It runs once per loaded engine and begins with a greedy 128-token probe pair. It then runs shape cells under a 20-second wall budget, using the artifact's default sampling. It trains no rates or counters. Startup preload runs before coordinator registration or before the standalone listener opens.

The supplied units are BASE text for lines 1638-2205 and do not include the new section. That section is visible only as a truncated patch excerpt, and the excerpt cuts off mid-sentence. I could not examine the rest of the added text or any implementing code, so this is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.

From the visible excerpt, no security-relevant behavior change is described:
- The warmup uses synthetic probes, not consumer data (A-001).
- It runs before registration, so routed traffic cannot reach it.
- It does not alter the attestation, authorization, or encryption flows (TB-002, TB-011, T-053).
- It does not touch the prefix-cache SSD tier (T-041), so the TTL, HMAC naming and DBK3 posture are unchanged.
- A local-endpoint request can still preempt the warmup, which is an availability note only.

The remaining base text I reviewed (MiMo native candidate, Flint, Bonsai) is unchanged context and shows no modification in this PR. One residual question for integration: whether the warmup's synthetic prompts could populate the encrypted SSD prefix cache or the resident prefix state. That would affect T-041 and routing-evidence epoch behavior, but the truncated excerpt does not say. Because the added text is truncated, I mark deeper review as warranted but low priority. No findings.
